newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close at fresh year high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close at fresh year high.

text.p: French shares closed at a fresh year high on Monday after the market resumed its advance following a brief pause early in the day to consolidate last week's gains.

Traders said rising bond prices and hopes of interest rate cuts in France and Germany as early as this week fuelled the advance on the bourse, which remained bullish despite an early loss on Wall Street.
Brokers said investors are hoping for big flows into the bourse in the new year from cash-rich U.S. funds.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 2.97 points or 0.13 percent at 2,318.63 -- just below a stubborn resistance level at 2,320 -- and the CAC-40 December futures contract rose three points to 2,322. Volume was 4.99 billion francs.
Some analysts expect the CAC to test its all time high of 2,360.98 points, set in February 1994, before the end of the year.

Pension funds are picking blue chips for year-end window-dressing, adding to the CAC index's gains. Legrand, up 1.1 percent at 915 francs, L'Oreal, up 0.73 percent at 1,925, LVMH, up 0.83 percent at 1,335, were among the beneficiaries.

Shares in Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere eased respectively 1.64 percent to 467 francs and 0.32 percent to 157.50 francs, pressured by uncertainties over the Thomson privatisation and GEC's demands on Alcatel for an equal share in the proposed Framatome GEC Alsthom merger.
Eurotunnel shares dropped 6.9 percent to 6.75 francs. Passenger service remains disrupted since a fire two weeks ago.

Lyonnaise des Eaux shares firmed 1.77 percent to 506 francs. A major French broker said a market news service reported that a big domestic bank downgraded the stock to reduce from add and that Lyonnaise could merge with Tractebel of Belgium through a share swap. Lyonnaise officials were not available for comment.

Shares in carmakers PSA Peugeot Citroen and Renault fell on a 21.7 percent drop in new car sales in France in November. The slide had been expected after a summer buying spree in the runup to the expiry on September 30 of a state rebate scheme. PSA Peugeot Citroen shares fell 0.62 percent to 638 francs. Renault shares slumped 3.31 percent to 119.90 francs.
